summary: Identical replayed conversational turns treated as cache misses due to prompt normalization key divergence
description: Issue summary: Several LexiChat customers report 100–300ms higher p50/p95 latency and intermittent p99 timeouts on follow-up conversational turns that should be served from the KV/prefix cache. Impact: user-facing latency regressions during multi-turn dialogs, elevated token costs due to cold-path decoding, and occasional 504s for long conversations. Environment: prod clusters in us-east with dedicated capacity for LexiChat (dedicated pool ID: dc-lexi-03). Observed behavior: Two subsequent identical prompts replayed by the LexiChat SDK are treated as distinct cache keys; first request warms the cache and completes in expected latency, the replay gets a cold-path KV lookup and shows increased latency or timeout. Expected behavior: byte-identical conversational turns should map to the same prefix/KV cache keys and be served from cache, producing consistent low latency for repeats.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LexiChat sandbox to send a multi-turn conversation to redwood-open-7b in prod/us-east (pool dc-lexi-03).
2) At turn N, send prompt text 'Summarize the last response:' (exact same bytes) and observe latency ~45ms.
3) Immediately replay the same prompt text as a follow-up request (same conversation id) and observe latency jump to 250–400ms or a 504 timeout in some cases.
4) Capture request traces, raw prompt bytes, and KV keys emitted by the serving-runtime for both requests.
5) Reproduce more reliably by toggling SDK option normalize_unicode=true/false.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:42:10Z request_id=tx-8a3f prefix_key=ab12... (from first request) latency=48ms route=dc-lexi-03 model=redwood-open-7b
Attached: redwood-serving-traces (trace ids: tr-20260312-615, tr-20260312-616) and a hex dump of prompt bytes for both requests.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: cache eviction or shard rebalance. Cluster metrics show no recent rebalances and shard occupancy stable.

Trace inspection: first/second requests show different prefix_key values despite identical visible prompt text. Raw byte dumps differ only in Unicode normalization forms (first used NFKC, second NFC).
Reproducer: toggling the SDK's normalize_unicode flag changes behavior; enabling normalization on client eliminates divergence and both requests hit the same key.

Root cause theory: recent tokenizer update (PR #4321) introduced a change in how prompt bytes are normalized before key derivation — server-side normalization now uses a different Unicode normalization form than older SDKs. When client and server disagree, semantically identical prompts produce distinct keys and miss the prefix cache.
Impact window: started ~2026-03-10 08:00 UTC correlating with rollout of serving-runtime v2.14.2 which included tokenizer normalization changes.
workaround: Ask LexiChat to enable client-side unicode normalization (NFKC) as a temporary measure; this restores key parity with current server-side behavior and reduces p99 latency. Applied to customer in prod pool dc-lexi-03 at 2026-03-12T17:00Z.
resolution_plan: 1) Roll a patch to serving-runtime to accept both normalization forms when deriving cache keys (backcompat shim) and log normalization form mismatches for visibility. 2) Coordinate a follow-up SDK release to align client normalization with server canonicalization. 3) Add a unit/integration test asserting identical visible prompts map to same cache key across normalization variants. Target: hotfix rollout to prod us-east by 2026-03-15.
